Hörl G, Kroisel PM, Wagner E, et al, 2006, Compound heterozygosity (G71R/R140H) in the lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) gene results in an intermediate phenotype between LCAT-deficiency and fish-eye disease, Atherosclerosis PMID:16216249

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: missense, NP_000220.1:p.(Gly95Arg). The papers describe the disease as autosomal recessive and caused by loss of LCAT function; the review also notes an intermediate (co-dominant) biochemical phenotype in heterozygous carriers.

quotes.quote: LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disease [4, 5].
Loss of LCAT function causes decreased maturation of HDL particles and increased HDL levels of unesterified cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine.

carriers of one mutant LCAT allele show an intermediate biochemical phenotype between homozygous carriers and controls, suggesting that the disease, which is reported as recessive, is indeed co-dominant for the biochemical phenotype.

concerns: The variant appears only in a systematic review table (34256778) without a case description; the review does not name the original publication in the row, so the person-level data are second-hand.
Zygosity, phase and family data are not given in the review; the batch row records zygosity as not reported.
A second LCAT variant (c.491G>A) is listed for the same person.
The compound-heterozygosity statement and the protein labels G71R/R140H come only from the title of a cited reference, in legacy (mature-protein) numbering; the review's own rows give no zygosity.
notes_for_panel: One unclassified Austrian male (author Horl) listed with c.283G>C and c.491G>A. The review's reference list includes Hörl et al. 2006, whose title reports compound heterozygosity G71R/R140H with an intermediate FLD/FED phenotype; these protein labels are 24 residues lower than the batch's predicted protein for c.283G>C (Gly95Arg), consistent with mature-protein numbering, but the review does not state the numbering or link the row to that reference. The Austrian row of Table 1 (4 cases) also lists both variants (cohort-level). Phase shown only through the cited title, not through data in this paper.
